lines.en: Otoha and I make it back to the party without drawing much attention to ourselves since I don’t think anyone here really expects me to fuck her.
Joke’s on them though because the time has come for me to put the moves on her.
: Hey.
: Yo.
She totally wants me.
I’ll leave it here for today, though. Especially since it looks like the time has come for another Christmas tradition of spin the-
: Alright, gals! Who’s ready for some Christmas karaoke featuring holiday classics like Ayane’s theme song, Despacito?!
: No. Do the other tradition. The one where you have to kiss each other.
: If it’ll make you feel better, I’ll go kiss Nodoka.
: Would you really?
: No. I just wanted to add onto your sadness. It gets me high.
: You’re a terrible friend.
: I’m a terrible girlfriend too, apparently.
: One day, you’re going to decide to settle down and make someone out there very miserable, Otoha.
: Aww, I’d be taking after you.
: Don’t just stare at me like that, Io! Grab a mic! You know the words!
: I don’t even know the language.
: Spanish!
: Just like your aunt!
: Don’t go rewriting people’s ethnicities while everyone is too busy to question them! Someone is going to hear that and think it’s true!
: ¡Canta conmigo, Io!
: ¡¿Puedo ir al baño por favor?!
: Yes! Why are you asking me?!
: Ha! So you do know Spanish! I caught you!
: Do you ever think about how weird everyone in our class is? Or are you too busy trying to figure out how you’re going to hook up with them?
: Those things are not mutually exclusive. I think of both all the time.
: Who’s the weirdest? If you had to rank them all.
: You. Easy.
: Me? I feel like I’m super normal by comparison.
: Yeah, that’s what makes you the weirdest. You somehow manage to stick out due to how inconspicuous and plain you are. It’s kind of impressive, actually.
: Does that mean you’re the most normal then?
: No. It means Yasu is the most normal.
: Then that is what I will take as the true answer to my question. Thank you for your cooperation. I will now be leaving.
: Really? You sure you don’t want to hang out for a little while longer? You’re supposed to be lonely.
: I am. I’m just gonna go be lonely all by myself. Or maybe with Nodoka or something? Stay tuned and you’ll find out.
: Fine. But I’m giving you a mission.
: No, I will not spike anyone’s drink for you.
: I just wanted you to go convince the girls to stop singing and start making out.
: I’ll see what I can do. How about you, though?
: I don’t know. I’ll probably just stand here and hallucinate or something. That’s how this normally goes.
: How what normally goes?
: Oh, god damn it.
: Where have you been, Malvin? I’ve been looking all over for you. Diamond keeps showing up and providing unsolicited advice in the voice of the student council president.
: Spork has been fed. A glutton, he is. So I have returned to provide you advice in place of Diamond!
: I hope the voice you’ve attributed to me doesn’t cause you as much pain as the student council one does.
: I think it’s best if we just don’t even talk about that. What should I do now, though? Go cause a misunderstanding? Pull someone into a dark room?
: No, idiot! Those are bad things! You’re a good guy deep down, Akira! We just need to figure out how to put you into a situation that won’t endanger anyone.
: Like talking to that one little girl who’s reading a book all by herself in the middle of a Christmas party.
: It’s true that I am supposed to be watching her. Are you sure no one’s being put in danger by me doing that, though? I’m not exactly trustworthy in...virtually any capacity whatsoever.
: Yeah! I know! But you’d never stoop that low, would you?
: Malvin-
: Go! Fulfill your duty! She looks so lonely, doesn’t she?
She really does. But this was always going to happen from the moment Tsubasa decided to leave her in my care rather than that of her ten thousand henchmen.
Tsukasa may be smart for her age. And in a lot of ways, she’s more mature than even I am. But she’s still just “Touka’s little sister” to everyone here.
So the only other person who might know how to handle her at all would be Chika, and I’m not sure Chika is mentally capable of handling anything other than my penis right now.
The thing is, though, I don’t fit in either. Or at least that’d be the case if Imani wasn’t here. But...she wasn’t for a long time. So I know how it feels to not belong.
I can relate to her in that respect. And...
And it’d probably make her happy if someone were to give her attention.
That always works for me.
: Hey. What are you doing all alone over here?
: Oh. Hi, Jeeves. I’m just trying to decipher some ancient runes that will help me cast a spell to make everyone care about me.
: Well, it seems to have worked on me.
: But I haven’t cast it yet.
: Well...right. I just figured that was more of a figure of speech than you actually trying to learn a spell.
: Why?
: Because...magic isn’t real?
: Then what am I?
: What are any of us?
: Jeeves, is Christmas really the time to get all philosophical like that?
: I am clearly very busy right now. And you clearly don’t want to be around me anyway since you’ve been running all over the place since you got here.
: I’m just going to read my spellbook and wait for Mother to text me back. I’m sure there will be a helicopter here to pick me up any minute now.
: I’m sorry. I’m not used to babysitting. I-
: No one here is being babysat, Jeeves. I’m perfectly capable of taking care of myself. I’m just...not familiar with any of the girls in your class, so we have nothing in common.
: Which is to be expected, of course. It doesn’t matter how much preparation and time I put into learning their customs if I have very little practical experience...well...practicing them.
: I can just hire other commoners to speak with for practice. And maybe, a few years from now, I’ll seem more...approachable.
: You can talk to me if you want. I don’t have anything else going on right now.
: You’re only saying that out of pity, aren’t you?
: Would you prefer if just no one came over to talk to you? Because, if you’re happy over here by yourself, I have no problem fucking off elsewhere.
: I suppose I wouldn’t mind if you just...also felt like sitting here.
: But the moment my helicopter shows up, don’t expect me to stick around. There is no amount of this strange Latin music that I would prefer over a night on the slopes.
: You learn to tune it out after a while. I probably wouldn’t expect a text or call if I were you though, Tsukasa.
: Why? Am I finally being put up for adoption?

: What? No. It’s just...your parents are supposed to be enjoying the holiday together, aren’t they? That’d be harder to do if they had to worry about you the whole time. They probably just want some privacy.
: For what?
: You know...things adults need privacy for.
: Sensei? What are-
: You mean like sexual intercourse?
: S- what on earth are you talking to my little sister about?!
: ...Skiing?
: As if I’m going to believe that!
: Jeeves is telling the truth, Onee-sama. We were just engaging in a discussion about why Mother and Father would require privacy for their ski trip.
: R...Regardless of whether or not it was warranted, you should know better than to broach that subject with just anyone, Tsukasa.
: But this isn’t anyone we’re talking about, Onee-sama. It’s Jeeves. I’m sure you’d have no problem discussing this subject with him, so why should I?
: Because it’s inappropriate. There’s a time and place for topics like that, and I can assure you that a Christmas party on Christmas is not one of them.
: Then how about we play a game instead?! Now that it’s all three of us!
: A...game? I do hope you’re not referring to the one involving the bottle that Otoha brought up to me a moment ago.
So she really is my friend after all.
: How about we play the game where we list the things we want for Christmas?! I’ve seen that show up in several Christmas-themed movies with Chinami.
: Is there actually a game like that?
: It’s not really a game. That’s just...kind of a thing some families and people do so that the totally real human man named Santa Claus knows what to deliver them.
: I guess neither of you two would really know about that, though, since you already have everything you could ever want.
: For this Christmas, I would like a teacher who does not view me as his mother.
: Imani exists. It’s a Christmas miracle.
: And I want Onee-sama’s favorite horse!
: I will cut you into pieces, you petulant whelp.
: Hahaha! Isn’t Onee-sama funny when she makes that face, Jeeves?!
: Woah.
: Ahem.
: How strange. I have no idea what came over me just now. Apologies for that rather uncouth display, Sensei.
: Onee-sama always does that when I make jokes about Apollo.
: Apollo?
: My beautiful, wonderful, spectacular and prized Misaki. Though, it was my mother who named him and not me.
: Regardless, you have been warned many times in the past to never speak that name, Tsukasa. You are unworthy.
: That’s fine. All I really want for Christmas is to better understand poor people, anyway.
: Well, that’s a rather simple wish. Isn’t it?
: Like Jeeves said — we already have everything else. So if I’m going to wish for anything, it sort of has to be something immaterial, right?
: I suppose that’s true. But becoming accustomed to the way things work on the outside takes a great deal more than just a wish, Tsukasa.
: The totally real human man named Santa Claus won’t be able to simply place vague concepts and constructs beneath all of our trees.
: You guys...get presents underneath all of your trees? I’ve seen like fifty.
: And yet none of them reserve a place for Tsukasa’s wish.
: I just think it’d be nice to understand more people so I don’t accidentally make Jeeves feel like a loser anymore.
: I would appreciate that. Thanks, Tsukasa.
: You’re welcome, loser.
: Oh, okay. So you’re totally cool with making me feel like a loser on purpose then.
: Yeah, that’s a different thing. And besides, I’m sure Santa can figure it out! And if he doesn’t, I’ll just ask Father to give him a raise. Santa Claus is probably on Tsukioka payroll, right?
: Tsukasa...what exactly would you gain from such a thing in the first place?
: Huh? What do you mean?
: Just...the amount of time and energy you’re dedicating to understanding people you won’t ever come into contact with seems rather strange, does it not?
: Apart from Sensei and Chinami, you barely speak to “commoners” at all. And you’ll rarely ever need to since I am the heir to the family business.
: You’re free to live a life of ease. Why bother making things more difficult for yourself in order to fit into a world you clearly don’t belong in?
: Don’t...belong in?
: Touka, come on. You could have worded that better.
: I’m merely trying to protect her, Sensei. And while I’m absolutely not saying Tsukasa doesn’t belong in your world, I don’t think it’s absurd to say she “doesn’t belong” in your world.
: We’re lucky enough to come from a family that already possesses all the resources we could ever need.
: And while I’ve absolutely grown to love many people outside of our bubble, I am challenged by that love every single day.
: We simply don’t fit in here. And I fail to understand the value Tsukasa places in chasing after hardship when a mere Christmas party is enough to cast such a look on her face.
: Touka...that’s-
: No...she’s right.
: Nobody wants me here.
: No one’s tried to talk to me...and the only reason you two came over in the first place was to keep me company out of pity.
: I know I don’t fit in out there...but I don’t fit in here either.
: So...where do I belong then?
: Tsukasa-
: I just remembered I...I have to clean my room.
: You...Do you even know how to clean?...
: I’ll figure it out.
: Goodbye, Jeeves...thanks for coming over to talk to me.
: I hope you get everything you want for Christmas.
Touka and I stand there, unsure of what to do as Tsukasa leaves the room.
We both know that I’m we’re supposed to be keeping an eye on her for...whatever reason Tsubasa is trying to keep her away from their meeting...
But we also know it would be wrong to just keep her here if she’s feeling uncomfortable.
Touka is clearly conflicted — like she wants to chase after her and tell her that she is wanted here.
She just can’t...
Because she’s always been a terrible liar.
And she probably just think she’ll make it worse.
Tsukasa’s affection has increased to [tsukasa_love]!
: Goodbye, Jeeves...thanks for coming over to-
: Where do you think you’re going?
: Huh? To...clean my room. I just said-
: Yeah, I know what you said. But I want you here. Touka’s just not very good at getting her point across when it comes to you.
: Yes, I...I never intended to make you feel unwanted, Tsukasa. I just don’t want you to have to struggle if there are ways around-
: I’ve got it from here, Touka. Thanks.
: Oh. Oh, I’ll...okay.
: I suppose I’ll just...go check on Yasu then.
Touka gets up and walks away, leaving me alone with my latest pupil and whoever else is smart enough to keep an eye on me while I’m alone with her.
: You okay? You know she didn’t mean any of that-
: You...stood up for me.
: I...guess I did. Yeah.
: Why?
: What do you mean “why?” I didn’t want you getting upset and wandering off over a misunderstanding.
: But it wasn’t a misunderstanding.
: I’m not an idiot, Jeeves. I can tell when people don’t want to be around me. And the only people here who have even noticed me at all are you and Onee-sama.
: I don’t belong here...or there or...anywhere. That’s how afterthoughts work and...that’s what I am.
: Even on Christmas, I’ve been pawned off on you like...some kind of unwanted toy. And Mother says it’s because of a ski trip, but...
: Tsukasa, shut up.
: Did you just...tell me to shut up? Who do you think you are?
: Your tutor. And frankly, you should be glad that I’m still taking the time to instruct you while neglecting my duties at the school.
: I am...
: I don’t...
: I’m not really...
: I’ve never...
: Thank you...
: There’s no need to thank me. I just know what it’s like to be in your shoes.
: You know what it’s like to be extremely rich and talented?
: Uh...no. I know what it’s like to be among a bunch of people you’re completely different from. And so does your sister — which is why she worries about you.
: Onee-sama doesn’t worry about me...
: She thinks I’m a burden too.
: But you, Jeeves...
: You...make me feel like...somebody actually does want me sometimes.
: If you’re being paid for it, you’re very good at your job.
: I’m not being paid for it, Tsukasa. You’re just...not the burden you think you are.
: I really do think I...need to go clean my room...
: Tsukasa-
: I’m happy, though...I’m not doing it because I feel sad or left out anymore.
: Then why would-
: I just...um...
: I know that...
: I think...things can only go down from here...
: Goodnight, Jeeves...and Merry Christmas.
: I didn’t get what I wanted, but...
: This was just as good.
I watch Tsukasa as she walks away.
Touka notices and does the same, but doesn’t chase after her.
I think both of us are just surprised to see her look so...different all of a sudden.
For Touka, I think that might be a good thing.
For me, though?
It’s Hell.
Tsukasa’s affection has increased by 10!
